We need to fix compilation errors: missing MockitoExtension import. We can remove Mockito usage. The test class uses @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) but not using any Mockito features. We can replace with no extension, or use JUnit's extension for nothing. Simplest: remove import and annotation. So delete import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension; and @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) line.

Also need to ensure other imports are correct. Already have import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*; import com.networknt.schema.SpecVersion.VersionFlag; import java.lang.reflect.Field; import org.junit.jupiter.api.*; import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith; but we will remove ExtendWith import if not used. Actually we can keep ExtendWith import but not used; but better remove.

Thus final code: package line, imports: static assertions, SpecVersion.VersionFlag, java.lang.reflect.Field, org.junit.jupiter.api.*; maybe also import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith removed.

Now test class without annotation.

Check any other compile issues: The code uses SchemaValidatorsConfig.builder().discriminatorKeywordEnabled(...).nullableKeywordEnabled(...).build(); Ensure builder methods exist. Assume library.

Also uses JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(VersionFlag.V202012); This method exists.

Potential issue: In disabledConfig building line they used comment after method call with // also disabled to verify it gets enabled automatically . In code they wrote:

SchemaValidatorsConfig disabledConfig = SchemaValidatorsConfig.builder().discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false).// also disabled to verify it gets enabled automatically
        nullableKeywordEnabled(false).build();

This line has comment after dot which may cause syntax error because comment placed after dot? Actually they wrote .discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false).// also disabled ... newline then nullableKeywordEnabled(false).build();

In Java, after a dot you can have a comment? The comment starts with // and goes to end of line, so the dot before comment is fine, but the comment after dot means the dot is before comment, then newline, then nullableKeywordEnabled. The dot is part of method chain, but comment inserted after dot may break because the dot is before comment, then newline, then whitespace then nullableKeywordEnabled. The dot is not attached to the next token, but that's okay because dot is an operator requiring a following identifier; comment ends line, newline, then whitespace then nullableKeywordEnabled; the dot is still there before comment, but after comment there is newline, so the dot is not attached to identifier, causing compile error: " '.' expected " maybe. Actually code: .discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false).// also disabled ... newline whitespace nullableKeywordEnabled... The dot before comment is fine, but after comment there is no identifier; the dot before comment belongs to the chain, but after comment there is newline and then whitespace then nullableKeywordEnabled, but there is no dot before nullableKeywordEnabled. The dot before comment is consumed, but after comment we need a dot to continue chain. In the original they had .discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false). // comment newline nullableKeywordEnabled... The dot before comment ends the method call, then dot after comment is missing. Actually they have .discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false).// comment newline nullableKeywordEnabled... The dot before comment is the dot that separates the previous method call from the next; but they placed comment after the dot, which means the dot is still there, but the comment consumes rest of line, but the dot is before comment, so dot is present. After comment line ends, the next line starts with whitespace then nullableKeywordEnabled, but there is no dot preceding it because dot already used? The dot is before comment, not after; the dot is already placed, so the next token should be the method name, which is nullableKeywordEnabled, but there is no dot now because dot already consumed. Actually syntax: expression . identifier . // comment newline identifier ... The dot before comment is part of the chain, then comment, then newline, then identifier. That should be okay because dot is before comment, then comment ends line, but dot is still there preceding comment; after comment line ends, the parser expects the identifier after dot, but it's on next line; whitespace and newline are ignored, identifier appears. So it should compile. Might be fine.

But there is also similar comment after .discriminatorKeywordEnabled(false).// keep nullable the same to isolate the change newline nullableKeywordEnabled(true).build();

Same pattern.

Thus only missing Mockito import.

Also need to remove @ExtendWith annotation line.

Let's produce corrected code.
